verdicts.reason: Quote states full write/read access to all 32 bits via direct access.
Mask/data split and no RMW stated.
Read returns half of DATA_OUT with zero upper bits.
Software usage guidance; nothing for hardware to verify (DATA_IN behaviour covered elsewhere).
Quote states DATA_OE duplicates the concept with direct and masked access.

Pad control block is outside the GPIO; output enable routing is a description. Cannot be exercised in the GPIO test alone; an output-enable-to-pad connection is only observable at the interface, so at best an assertion on oe output.
Quote explicitly states unused outputs have no effect on input.
Aliasing and per-pin write isolation stated.
Register layout stated by quote.

Requirement on write coverage is about the bus access granularity; the register enforces it (access cannot be granted to partial fields). Actor master is a software/bus constraint; better expressed as a slave/interconnect behaviour, but the quote is a rule for the writer.
Design rationale; the separate registers are already covered by the address layout rule GP-T3.2.2-02.
Quote states no per-pin view for these registers.
DATA_IN always readable and reflects pad regardless of OE.
Quote states tie-off to zero when not connected.
Optional per-input filter enabled by CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER.
Strap sampling timing stated by quote.
Sampling only once, all 32 bits regardless of OE.
General description of 32 interrupts; specifics are in other rules.

Rule mixes two statements; 'only triggered by GPIO input' is a restriction (MUST_NOT-like for other sources) but the enablement requirement is stated. Quote supports it as written with the state readable only if enabled; keep MUST but check both scenario and assertion is not feasible.
W1C clearing stated.
Four interrupt types stated.
Both-edge configuration allowed, stated as 'in theory'.
Noise filter precedes interrupt detection per Note #2.
Level interrupt conversion stated.

questions.question: Is the interrupt noise filter path (CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER) optional per input, and how does the 'MUST pass through filter' rule relate to it being optional?
Does INTR_STATE only show an interrupt when both INTR_ENABLE and an INTR_CTRL_EN bit are set, or does INTR_ENABLE only gate the output interrupt?
